headline: The U.S. Army has announced that it has awarded Hanwha Defense USA, the American subsidiary of South Korean Hanwha Group, a contract to procure an initial batch of K9MH 155mm/52-caliber self-propelled howitzers on a wheeled chassis under the Mobile Tactical Cannon (MTC) program. The K9MH uses a Tatra 8×8 wheeled chassis. The MTC program calls for the eventual procurement of a new 155mm/52-caliber wheeled self-propelled howitzer to replace the U.S. Army’s 155mm/39-caliber M777A2 lightweight towed howitzers. The contract with Hanwha Defense USA covers the delivery of six K9MH prototypes to the U.S. Army for $100.3 million, with an option for an additional 12 prototypes. If the option is exercised, the total contract value could increase to $262.9 million. The K9MH howitzers will be used in a four-year evaluation and testing phase. In addition to Hanwha Defense USA’s K9MH, other 155mm/52-caliber wheeled self-propelled howitzers competing under the MTC program include the SIGMA, proposed by a consortium of Elbit America, Anduril, and Oshkosh Defense; the CAESAR, proposed by Leonardo DRS and KNDS; the RCH 155 from Rheinmetall; and the Archer from BAE Systems. Hanwha is proposing to produce the K9MH for the U.S. Army at its new facility currently under construction in Opelika, Alabama. However, despite the K9MH’s formal selection under the MTC program, it is by no means certain that the system will ultimately enter U.S. Army service.
summary: The U.S. Army has announced that it has awarded Hanwha Defense USA, the American subsidiary of South Korean Hanwha Group, a contract to procure an initial batch of K9MH 155mm/52-caliber self-propelled howitzers on a wheeled chassis under the Mobile Tactical Cannon (MTC) program.

headline: The U.S. Navy has publicly disclosed a previously unannounced AIM-424 Long Range Air-to-Air Missile (LRAAM), also known as the "Malice", revealing the weapon mounted inside the internal weapons bay of an F-35C Lightning II with an AIM-120 AMRAAM mounted on the bay door. The Navy describes the AIM-424 as its next-generation, long range air to air missile, intended to give Navy and Marine Corps aviators greater capability against advanced threats. The internal carriage is particularly significant. Rather than simply adding another externally carried long-range missile, the AIM-424 appears to have been designed around the F-35's limited internal weapons-bay dimensions, allowing the aircraft to retain its low-observable configuration while carrying a substantially longer-range air-to-air weapon. The missile is still associated with testing and development, and the Navy has released few technical details regarding its range, seeker, propulsion or intended employment. The available imagery does, however, show the AIM-424 being evaluated on both the F-35C and F/A-18E/F, indicating that the weapon is being considered across the Navy's carrier aviation force. Source: https://www.dvidshub.net/image/9879420/aim-424-long-range-air-air-missile-lraam

headline: The USS Abraham Lincoln (CVN-72) has left the Middle East after 274 days deployed, with the carrier strike group now operating in the Indian Ocean under U.S. 7th Fleet, according to USNI. The carrier departed San Diego on Nov. 25 and has been at sea since its last port visit in Guam on Dec. 11—more than eight months without a port call, breaking the previous 206-day record set by USS Dwight D. Eisenhower during the COVID-19 pandemic. The unusually long deployment was compounded by the loss of regional logistics hubs following Iranian attacks, forcing Navy supply ships to travel thousands of miles to sustain the carrier and other forces operating in the Arabian Sea. The Navy says resupply problems improved after new supply lines were established. Lincoln is being replaced in the region by the forward deployed USS George Washington (CVN-73), which arrived two days ago and will join USS George H.W. Bush (CVN-77) to maintain a two carrier presence amid the war with Iran. From the Western Indian Ocean, it will take Lincoln 3-4 weeks to transit across the Pacific back to San Diego. An open question is whether the ship will make a port call on the way home, which would extend the deployment a few days. The Navy is now dealing with a broader pattern of extended deployments: USNI notes that carrier deployments since October 2023 have averaged about 8½ months, while USS Gerald R. headline: According to the Wall Street Journal, Army Secretary Dan Driscoll is expected to leave his post by the end of the year, or possibly sooner, after months of reported tension with Secretary of War Pete Hegseth. Driscoll has served about 18 months and developed a close working relationship with former Army Chief of Staff Gen. Randy George. The two pushed the Army toward greater use of commercial technology and lessons from Ukraine, including integrating commercially available systems more rapidly into military operations. George was abruptly fired by Hegseth in April and has not been replaced by a Senate-confirmed successor. Gen. Christopher LaNeve is currently serving as acting Army chief of staff. Driscoll's departure would therefore leave both of the Army's top civilian and uniformed leadership positions without Senate-confirmed permanent leaders. The reported split also appears to reflect a broader disagreement over Army transformation. Driscoll had advocated adopting Ukrainian style approaches to commercial technology and battlefield innovation, while his relationship with Hegseth reportedly deteriorated after Driscoll became involved in efforts to arrange senior level visits and Army reform discussions. There has been no official confirmation of Driscoll's departure. The Pentagon and Driscoll's representatives declined to comment. Source: https://www.wsj.com/politics/national-security/army-secretary-expected-to-step-down-by-years-end-d7477efb

headline: Federal prosecutors say an Albany, New York, woman was arrested after allegedly developing a plan to attack the New York State Capitol and kill state senators in the name of ISIS. According to the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of New York, Jessica Bowie, 35, was arrested Aug. 19 after taking possession of what she believed was an explosive device. Investigators allege she had sworn allegiance to ISIS, photographed the Capitol and discussed destroying the building, killing lawmakers and disrupting the U.S. government. The complaint also alleges Bowie expressed support for al-Qaeda's 9/11 attacks online, threatened to poison Americans and recorded and distributed a formal bay'ah, or oath of allegiance, to ISIS. Prosecutors say the alleged plan went beyond rhetoric: investigators allege Bowie intended to attack the Capitol and then flee to join ISIS controlled territory. The device she obtained was apparently part of the FBI's effort to identify and disrupt the alleged plot before an attack could occur. Bowie was charged with attempting to provide material support to a designated foreign terrorist organization, a federal offense carrying a maximum sentence of 20 years. She was ordered detained pending further proceedings.

headline: The FBI has raided former Rep. Eric Swalwell’s Washington home and seized electronic devices at San Francisco airport as part of a federal investigation into sexual assault allegations against him. The raid comes after Swalwell resigned from Congress and ended his campaign for governor of California in April following multiple allegations of sexual misconduct. The Manhattan DA and Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department are also investigating. Swalwell was previously linked to Christine Fang, or “Fang Fang,” a Chinese national investigated by the FBI as a suspected Chinese intelligence operative who had cultivated relationships with politically promising Bay Area politicians. Newly released FBI documents reportedly show Swalwell acknowledged having a sexual relationship with Fang between 2012 and 2015. Swalwell was briefed by U.S. intelligence about concerns surrounding Fang, cut off contact with her and cooperated with the FBI. He was never charged with wrongdoing, and the House Ethics Committee ultimately closed its investigation without action. Swalwell has denied the sexual-assault allegations.
